title: A headlight or turn signal is out
h1: Why is one of my car's lights out?
metaDesc: Headlight out, turn signal blinking fast, or a small bulb dead? What to do first, how to find the cause, and when it's more than a bulb.
intro: A light that's out makes it harder to see or to be seen. Most of the time it's a bulb, but not always. Answer a few questions to find out how urgent it is and what to check.
safety: If both headlights go out at night, turn on your hazard lights, slow down and get off the road as soon as it's safe.
If your brake lights don't work, drivers behind you can't tell you're stopping. Get them fixed before you drive again.
If a turn signal doesn't work, use hand signals until it's fixed.
If you smell burning plastic or see smoke near a light, turn off the car and step away.

opts.a: One headlight, on low beam or high beam
A turn signal, or the turn signal blinks fast
A taillight, license plate light or another small light

q_one_headlight.help: Low beams are your normal headlights. High beams are the brighter setting you turn on with the stalk.

opts.a: It's out on one setting but works on the other, or it's simply dark
It flickers, or comes back when I tap it or hit a bump
It's an LED headlight, or a new bulb didn't fix it

q_signal.q: What does the turn signal do?
q_signal.help: The ticking you hear and the arrow on the dash blink at the same speed as the outside lights.

opts.a: It blinks much faster than normal on one side
Nothing blinks on either side, and the hazard lights don't work either
The arrow stays on without blinking, or doesn't light up

result.title: Both headlights out usually means a fuse, relay, switch or power problem
result.now: If it's dark, don't drive. Turn on your hazard lights and get off the road as soon as it's safe. Have it towed or have a mechanic come to you.
if: If it's daylight, check the headlight fuses and the headlight switch setting (turn it from Auto to On). Don't drive after dark until they work.
If other things are dimming or acting up too, the charging system may be failing. Pull over and turn off the engine.
If you smell burning plastic, turn off the car and step away.
result.why: Two bulbs rarely burn out at the same moment. When both go out together, something they share has failed, like a fuse, a relay, the switch or the power feed.

causes.name: Blown headlight fuse or bad relay
causes.clues: Both went out at once.

causes.name: Headlight switch or auto-light sensor fault
causes.clues: The dash lights work, but the headlights don't.

causes.name: Charging system or main power problem
causes.clues: The battery light is on, or other things are dimming.

you: Check the headlight fuses in the owner's manual.
Try the high beams and the flash-to-pass.

result.title: A headlight bulb has probably burned out
result.now: Replace the bulb. The owner's manual lists the bulb type and shows how to reach it. Until it's fixed, avoid driving at night if you can.
if: If you must drive at night, take well-lit roads and drive slower. Other drivers may think you're a motorcycle.
If a new bulb doesn't work, check the fuse and the plug behind the headlight.
Replacing headlight bulbs in pairs keeps both sides equally bright.
result.why: Headlight bulbs wear out. Some cars use one bulb for low and high beam, and others use separate bulbs, so one setting can fail while the other still works.

causes.name: Burned-out bulb
causes.clues: The light is dark, and it's been a few years.

causes.name: Loose or corroded plug behind the light
causes.clues: It flickered before it went out.

causes.name: Blown fuse for that side
causes.clues: A new bulb doesn't work.

you: Look at the bulb for a broken wire inside or a dark spot.
Check the plug behind the headlight.

result.title: A loose plug or worn socket is likely
result.now: Book a check when convenient. If you're comfortable, unplug and firmly reconnect the plug behind the headlight with the lights off.
if: If the plug or socket looks melted or brown, don't keep using that light. Have the socket replaced.
If it goes out while you're driving at night, slow down and use your high beams only if no one is ahead of or coming toward you.
result.why: Lights that flicker or come back after a bump usually have a poor connection. Heat from the bulb can damage the socket over time.

causes.name: Loose or corroded bulb plug
causes.clues: It comes back when you tap the light.

causes.name: Heat-damaged socket
causes.clues: The plug looks brown or melted.

causes.name: Broken wire
causes.clues: It changes when you turn the steering wheel or hit bumps.

you: Check the plug behind the headlight.

result.title: The headlight unit or its wiring may have failed
result.now: Book a check when convenient and avoid driving at night until it works. LED headlights often can't be fixed by changing a bulb.
if: If both sides go out, don't drive at night until it's fixed.
If a headlight warning appears on the dash, tell the shop.
result.why: Many newer cars use LED headlights that are built into the headlight housing. When they fail, the light module or its driver usually needs replacing, not a bulb.

causes.name: Failed LED module or driver
causes.clues: The car has LED headlights.

causes.name: Wiring or fuse problem
causes.clues: A new bulb didn't help.

causes.name: Water inside the headlight
causes.clues: You can see fog or droplets inside the lens.

you: Look for water inside the lens.
Check for open recalls using your VIN.

result.title: A turn signal bulb is probably out on that side
result.now: Turn on the turn signal and walk around the car. Check the front, rear and side signal lights on that side, then replace the dead bulb.
if: If all bulbs work but it still blinks fast, check the sockets for corrosion, or have the wiring checked.
If you put in LED bulbs recently, fast blinking can happen. The right bulb for your car is in the owner's manual.
Use hand signals until it's fixed.
result.why: Many cars blink fast on purpose when a signal bulb is out, to warn you that other drivers can't see your signal.

causes.name: Burned-out signal bulb
causes.clues: Fast blinking on one side only.

causes.name: Corroded socket or bad connection
causes.clues: The bulb looks fine but works on and off.

causes.name: Wrong bulb type
causes.clues: It started after a bulb change.

you: Check every signal light on that side.

result.title: The turn signal flasher, fuse or switch may have failed
result.now: Use hand signals and get it checked within a few days. Check the turn signal and hazard fuse first.
if: If the hazard lights also don't work, you can't warn others if you break down. Get it fixed soon.
If the brake lights also don't work, don't drive until it's fixed.
result.why: When no signal works on either side, the problem is in a part they share, like the flasher relay, a fuse, or the signal switch.

causes.name: Blown fuse
causes.clues: Signals and hazards both stopped.

causes.name: Failed flasher relay or module
causes.clues: No ticking sound at all.

causes.name: Worn turn signal switch
causes.clues: Hazards work, but signals don't.

you: Check the turn signal and hazard fuses.

result.title: Brake lights out: get them fixed before you drive
result.now: Have someone stand behind the car while you press the brake, or back up to a window and look for the glow. Our "Brake lights not working" guide walks through the checks.
if: If none of the brake lights work, don't drive until it's fixed. Drivers behind you won't know you're stopping.
If you also can't shift out of Park, the brake light switch is a likely cause.
result.why: When one brake light is out, it's usually a bulb. When all are out, a fuse or the switch at the brake pedal is more likely.

causes.name: Burned-out bulb
causes.clues: Only one side is dark.

causes.name: Brake light switch or fuse
causes.clues: All brake lights are dark.

you: Check each brake light, including the high center one.

result.title: A small bulb is out. Usually a simple fix
result.now: Replace the bulb. The owner's manual shows the bulb type and how to reach it.
if: If a whole group of lights is out, like the taillights on both sides, check the fuse.
If you see water inside the light, the seal may be leaking and the new bulb may fail again.
result.why: Taillights, license plate lights and side markers use small bulbs that burn out over time. A dead one can still get you pulled over.

causes.name: Burned-out bulb
causes.clues: Only one light is dark.

causes.name: Blown fuse
causes.clues: Several lights went out together.

causes.name: Water in the light
causes.clues: Fog or water inside the lens.

you: Check the fuse if several are out.

result.title: Do a quick walk-around to find the dead light
result.now: Park somewhere safe, turn on the headlights and hazard lights, and walk around the car. Ask someone to press the brake while you look at the back.
if: If both headlights are out, don't drive after dark until they work.
If no brake lights work, don't drive until they're fixed.
result.why: Knowing which light is out tells you how urgent it is. A license plate light is a small fix. Headlights and brake lights are about being safe on the road.

causes.name: Burned-out bulb
causes.clues: One light is dark.

causes.name: Fuse or switch
causes.clues: A whole group of lights is out.

you: Check every light with a helper.
